question: According to the Commission, there are around 16 million international families in the EU. When they break up, this gives rise to complex cross-border disputes regarding custody, parental responsibility and the recognition of decisions, which directly affect the rights of the child.

In its resolution of 5 April 2022 (2021/2060(INI)), Parliament called on the Commission to put forward a proposal for a regulation on cross-border mediation in cases concerning children, as well as to establish a European mediation certificate and common guidelines on the hearing of the child. The Commission did not give a specific response to the resolution. 1.
What steps has it taken since 2022 to follow up on those requests?
Does it intend to propose an instrument on cross-border mediation in cases concerning children, or a European mediation certificate? If not, why?
Has it assessed the application of Article 25 of the Brussels IIb Regulation as regards mediation?
